summary: Classify explicit Dutch imperatives as execution-authorized
description: The public Go router recognizes several Dutch and English imperatives but misses “los”. As a result, an explicit order such as “Los het probleem duurzaam op” is downgraded to advice. Add regression coverage and documentation for this Dutch imperative while preserving explicit advice/read-only/plan precedence.
acceptance: “Los het probleem duurzaam op” returns execute authority from imperative source, selects route goal on a valid repo with open work, and authorizes implementation.
Dutch advisory questions remain advice; explicit read-only and plan-only wording still overrides imperative verbs.
The public router recommendation preserves selected route and authority fields, and the Dutch imperative is documented in the router contract.

Negative Dutch forms with `niet`, `nooit`, or `onder geen beding`, and compound/contrast forms with conjunctions such as `en`/`én`, remain non-executing; restate them as a simple positive direct-object command ending in `op`.
